settings.heading:
The right mattress
for your IKEA frame.
settings.lede: IKEA King is 160 x 200cm. British King is 150 x 200cm. They are not the same, which is why nothing in a UK bed shop fits your bed properly.

settings.heading: The 10cm problem
settings.body:
If you bought a bed frame from IKEA, or almost anywhere in continental Europe, it takes a 160 x 200cm mattress.

Every British manufacturer builds 150 x 200. Put one in a European frame and you get a 10cm gap down one side, sheets that will not sit, and a mattress that shifts every time you move.

The usual answers are to buy IKEA's own mattress, import one from Europe and wait, or replace the frame. We make a third option.

settings.heading: The exact size
settings.text: 160 x 200cm, made to order. It fits the frame you already own.

settings.heading: 37cm of mattress
settings.text: Hand-assembled pocket sprung core with a comfort layer above it. Roughly twice the depth of what came with the frame.

settings.heading: A layer you can replace
settings.text: The part that wears out unzips and lifts off. [layer] to renew, not [price].

settings.label: Comfort layer
settings.text: Removable and reversible. Firm one side, soft the other. You do not choose - it arrives with both.

settings.text: Takes standard European King linen, widely available online.

settings.heading: Specification
settings.promise_body: Your mattress arrives with two feels in one layer - medium on one face, medium firm on the other. If neither is right, we send a complimentary comfort layer at a different tension, worth [layer]. If that still does not settle it, we collect the mattress and refund you in full.
